key_insight: EVATok adaptively assigns variable-length discrete token sequences across a video's temporal blocks, allocating more tokens to dynamic/complex segments and fewer to static/repetitive ones, thereby preserving reconstruction quality while reducing autoregressive generation cost.
problem_solved: Fixed-rate video tokenizers waste tokens on simple frames and underrepresent complex ones, forcing a trade-off between reconstruction fidelity and generation efficiency for autoregressive video models.
method: Learn a per-block complexity estimator that predicts token budget based on motion/visual complexity and content redundancy.
Use a variable-length tokenization pipeline (e.g., adaptive VQ/VAE or entropy-constrained quantization) that emits more discrete tokens for high-complexity blocks and fewer for low-complexity blocks.
Train end-to-end with reconstruction + budget/bitrate regularization and integrate the adaptive tokens into standard autoregressive generators for efficient sampling.
impact: Practitioners can substantially cut computation and sampling latency of autoregressive video generation without sacrificing visual quality, enabling more scalable training and deployment of high-fidelity video models.
visual_elements: Before/After timeline showing uniform vs adaptive token counts per frame (heatmap over time) with corresponding reconstruction frames.
Trade-off plot: reconstruction quality (PSNR/LPIPS) vs token budget or sampling FLOPs comparing EVATok to uniform tokenizers.
System diagram: adaptive complexity estimator → variable-length tokenizer → autoregressive generator, annotated with token flow and training losses.
Bar chart of latency or compute (FLOPs, memory) for generation across baselines and EVATok.
paper_title: EVATok: Adaptive Length Video Tokenization for Efficient Visual Autoregressive Generation
paper_authors: Tianwei Xiong, Jun Hao Liew, Zilong Huang, Zhijie Lin, Jiashi Feng
